extracted.intended_audience: investors, media, and the general public (stakeholders in GE and GE HealthCare)
extracted.subtask_description: A corporate press release announcing the filing of a Form 10 registration statement and describing the planned spin-off of GE HealthCare, its strategy, organization, timeline, and investor-related disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of Form 10 registration statement
rubrics_metrics.description: GE announced the filing of the Form 10 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for the planned spin-off of its Healthcare division (to be called GE HealthCare).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the Form 10 is available on the SEC website and on GE’s investor-relations SEC filings page; the Form 10 filed on October 11, 2022 is subject to change and will be made final prior to the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of historical and pro forma financial information
rubrics_metrics.description: Downloadable historical financial and pro forma financial information are provided as an attachment to the press release and are available on GE’s spinoff resources page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachments (e.g., Excel) and SEC filings should be used to review financial details supporting the spin-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned spin-off tax treatment and distribution structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The planned spin-off of GE HealthCare is intended to be tax-free for GE and GE shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes; GE plans to distribute at least 80.1% of GE HealthCare’s common stock to GE’s shareholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shareholders do not need to take any action to receive shares; GE expects to retain a stake of 19.9 percent in GE HealthCare. Completion is subject to final approval from the GE Board of Directors and other customary conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected timeline for completion
rubrics_metrics.description: GE continues to expect to complete the planned spin-off in the first week of 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion remains subject to Board approval and other customary closing conditions; filings and dates may change prior to effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing and ticker for spun-off company
rubrics_metrics.description: GE HealthCare will list on The Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol 'GEHC'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Future updates to the Form 10 will be filed with the SEC and may be viewed as filings under GE HealthCare’s current name until effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic priority: Drive industry-leading precision innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: GE HealthCare expects to drive industry-leading precision innovation to deliver better outcomes for patients and customers, with opportunities driven by digitizing healthcare and connecting care across diagnostics, therapy, and monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This priority highlights focus on product innovation, digital solutions, and cross-pathway care; cited as a key expectation in the Form 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic priority: Accelerate growth
rubrics_metrics.description: GE HealthCare intends to accelerate growth through product leadership and commercial execution, investing in innovation, pursuing disciplined capital allocation, and enhancing commercial execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on sustainable growth amid strong global and end-market dynamics and disciplined capital allocation strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic priority: Optimize operating model
rubrics_metrics.description: GE HealthCare plans to optimize its operating model via a simplified, more decentralized structure, tailoring its business model as a standalone leader and leveraging lean principles and a purpose-driven culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes operational simplification and decentralization to enhance agility as a standalone company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business segment organization
rubrics_metrics.description: GE HealthCare will be organized into four business segments: Imaging; Ultrasound; Patient Care Solutions; and Pharmaceutical Diagnostics, each with specified product and solution areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment details: Imaging (CT, MR, molecular imaging, X‑ray, women’s health, image-guided therapies, enterprise imaging software, service capabilities, digital solutions); Ultrasound (consoles and probes, handheld devices, intraoperative imaging systems, visualization software, service capabilities, digital solutions); Patient Care Solutions (monitoring, anesthesia and respiratory care, maternal infant care, diagnostic cardiology, consumables, service, digital solutions); Pharmaceutical Diagnostics (contrast media and radiopharmaceuticals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition and governance emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: GE announced GE HealthCare’s first Board of Directors, described as bringing a strong mix of expertise, industry experience, and diverse perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board composition is presented as a governance strength supporting the standalone company and its strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt issuance plan and use of proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: GE HealthCare plans to issue debt securities, with proceeds expected to be used to pay down outstanding GE debt over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the capital-structure planning referenced in earlier communications and SEC filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor engagement and disclosure events
rubrics_metrics.description: GE HealthCare will host an investor day on December 8, 2022, where management will present growth strategies, financial outlook, and showcase innovative solutions; investors, media, and the public are invited to learn more at GE’s spinoff resources page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investor days and public materials are part of the company’s plan to communicate strategy and outlook to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-GAAP financial measures disclosure and reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The press release uses non-GAAP financial measures and states that certain data are considered 'non-GAAP financial measures' under SEC rules; reconciliations to the most directly comparable GAAP measures are included in GE Healthcare Holding LLC’s Form 10 registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-GAAP measures supplement GAAP disclosures and should not be considered alternatives to GAAP measures; reasons for use and reconciliations are provided in the Form 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-looking statements and enumerated uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: The document contains forward-looking statements and lists examples of uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ, including: (1) success in executing and completing asset dispositions or other transactions (timing, ability to satisfy closing conditions, expected proceeds); (2) changes in macroeconomic and market conditions and market volatility (COVID-19 impacts, recession risk, inflation, supply chain constraints, rising interest rates, commodity prices, exchange rates); and (3) de-leveraging and capital allocation plans (actions to reduce indebtedness, capital structures, timing/amount of dividends, share repurchases, organic investments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers are directed to GE’s important forward-looking statement information and SEC filings for details; GE does not undertake to update forward-looking statements.
